Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of a line segment and an arc of a semi-circle centered at $(4,0)$ with radius $1.$ Find the value of 
${\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-1,3]$ and the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [3,5].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+4)\cdot 2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =5+\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
